minimal_context: The student is asked to explain an academic concept in English during a Grade 10 CLIL lesson.
dialogue:
TUTOR: I have just spent some time explaining the three main stages of the water cycle. Now, I want you to explain the first stage, evaporation, in your own words.

STUDENT: Um... yes. The water... it gets hot.

TUTOR: What else can you tell me about it?

STUDENT: Ah... the sun... the sun makes the water... um... change.

TUTOR: Please continue.

STUDENT: So... um... it... the water is... ah... it becomes... um... gas. And... ah... it... it goes up. That's... um... all.

options.A: Secure and participate in family counseling through the Department of Human Services to address the student's needs outside of the CLIL classroom.
options.B: Include choice-making by allowing the student freedom in selecting their own reinforcers, setting appropriate goals, and tracking their progress during CLIL lessons.
options.C: Provide noncontingent attention throughout the CLIL lessons and ignore the hesitant speech and pauses that function to gain the teacher's attention.
options.D: Provide extra support to enhance the student's L2 proficiency, especially related to academic language, by offering small-class intensive bridging courses before or during CLIL instruction.
